text:
Predicates:
Alien(x) ::: x is an alien.
Extraterrestrial(x) ::: x is extraterrestrial.
FromMars(x) ::: x is from Mars.
Human(x) ::: x is human.
FromEarth(x) ::: x is from Earth.
Marvin ::: Marvin is a specific individual.
Premises:
∀x (Alien(x) → Extraterrestrial(x)) ::: All aliens are extraterrestrial.
∀x (FromMars(x) → Alien(x)) ::: If someone is from Mars, then they are aliens.
¬∃x (Extraterrestrial(x) ∧ Human(x)) ::: No extraterrestrial is human.
∀x (FromEarth(x) → Human(x)) ::: Everyone from Earth is a human.
¬(FromEarth(Marvin) ∧ FromMars(Marvin)) ::: Marvin cannot be from Earth and from Mars simultaneously.
∃x (¬FromEarth(x) → Extraterrestrial(x)) ::: If Marvin is not from Earth, then Marvin is an extraterrestrial.
Conclusion:
¬(Human(Marvin) ∨ FromMars(Marvin)) ::: Marvin is neither a human nor from Mars.
